claims.value: The frozen force fields name the Army of the Ohio and the Army of Tennessee without counts; the live field reads zero. Schofield says Reilly's brigade, supported by all of Cox's division, made the assault of the 6th against a line he judged an outer line not held in strong force. Cox says the works were strongly held by Bate's division (from prisoners) and that Hood had put part of Hardee's corps on the Sandtown road line. NPS adds the Fourteenth Corps.
claims.rationale: Formation statements that conflict on the defenders' strength; no count is inspected and none is adopted. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Inconclusive and the live page Indecisive. Schofield says Reilly's brigade retired with heavy loss and that the enemy abandoned the position that night for his main works; Cox says Hascall's crossing enfiladed Bate's line, which was abandoned in the night, and quotes Sherman calling the next day's advance a noisy but not a bloody battle. NPS says the Federals were repulsed and failed to break the railroad.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads Unknown; the live field reads 625 (US 400; CS 225). Cox gives Reilly's loss on the 6th as a little over three hundred, and Baird's loss in carrying the skirmish line on the 5th as 83 killed and wounded with 140 prisoners taken. Schofield's inspected passage gives no figure.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Cox's figures are partial and span two days; the live figures have no inspected basis.

open_questions: Palmer's, Baird's, Johnson's, Reilly's and Hascall's reports, Bate's and Hardee's accounts, Hood's report (a family for other records, with little on August 5-7) and the compiled returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Cox's Atlanta (Scribner, 1882) is a second: a retrospective Union history by the Twenty-third Corps division commander, drawing on official reports and memoirs, so it is not independent of them. Schofield's September 10, 1864 report, printed in Volume XXXVIII Part 2, is a third family (interested Union account). Official Records Series I Volume XXXVIII is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Campaign-wide strength and loss totals are context, not assigned to one record.
